title: Feijoada, beef only
skill: A bean stew for a crowd

notes.1: Fills one stockpot and feeds 10. Leftovers freeze well.

move.title: Black beans, three beefs, a slow pot
move.body: Feijoada is Brazil's Saturday feast: black beans stewed for hours with meats, served with rice, garlicky greens, and orange slices. Brazilian cooks use many different meats; this version uses beef only: oxtail for body, chuck, and an all-beef sausage. You'll trim the fat, brown the meats, simmer them with the beans until everything is tender, and skim the fat before it's served to a crowd.

why.title: Trim and skim the fat
why.body: The hard white fat on beef is set apart in the law (Leviticus 3:17). Trim the thick fat from the oxtail and chuck before cooking, and skim what renders off the top of the pot.

why.title: Brown the meat
why.body: Browning in batches builds a dark crust and a fond in the pot, which flavors the beans.

why.title: Oxtail for body
why.body: Oxtail's joints melt into gelatin over hours, thickening the stew. It's done when the meat pulls from the bone.

why.title: Hold it hot
why.body: For a crowd, keep the pot at 140°F or above on low heat, or cool it fast and reheat to 165°F.

wrong.sign: There's a layer of fat on top
wrong.fix: Skim it off with a ladle, or chill the pot and lift off the set fat.
It needs longer. Simmer 30 minutes more and test again.

wrong.sign: The beans are breaking down before the meat is tender
wrong.fix: Lift the meat out, cool the beans, and finish the meat alone, then combine.

quiz.q: Why trim and skim the beef fat?
choices: The hard fat of beef is set apart in the law
The meat pulls from the bone

quiz.q: How hot must a stew be held for a crowd?
quiz.explain: Or cool fast and reheat to 165°F.

steps.text: The night before, pick over and rinse the beans and soak them in cold water.
Trim the thick white fat from the oxtail and the chuck. Pat the meat dry and season it with the salt and pepper.
Wash the board, knife, and your hands.
Brown the oxtail and chuck in the oil in the stockpot over medium-high heat, in batches, on all sides. Set them aside.
Wash the tongs and your hands.
Brown the kielbasa in the same pot, then add the diced onions and minced garlic and cook until soft, scraping up the fond.
Add the drained beans, the beans' water, the bay leaves, and the browned beef. Bring to a boil, skim, and simmer partly covered, stirring now and then.
steps.tip: Add hot water if the beans poke above the liquid.

steps.text: Check the chuck and the oxtail.
steps.tip: Fork-tender meat reads about 195°F; the oxtail pulls from the bone.

steps.text: Turn off the heat, let it settle 10 minutes, and ladle off the fat from the surface. Mash a ladle of beans against the pot to thicken.
While it settles, cook the rice by absorption, and slice the collards into thin ribbons and sauté them with olive oil and a little garlic until bright. Slice the oranges.
Serve the feijoada over rice with the greens and orange slices. Hold the pot at 140°F or above on low.
steps.look: Thick, dark, and glossy, no fat pooling on top.
